name: Creamware, neoclassical
summary: Cream-coloured lead-glazed earthenware that is light, cheap and strong. Potters in Staffordshire and Leeds make plain, classical forms with a feather edge or pierced work, and sell it to every table in Europe.

philosophy.core_thesis: A light cream body and a clear glaze, in a plain classical form, outsell both porcelain and delftware, because the whole service is cheap, even and easy to match.
design_principles: Fire a body of flint and white clay to a cream earthenware at 1100 °C.
Dip the piece in a clear lead glaze that fires to a pale yellow-cream gloss.
Keep the form plain and balanced: a circle, a straight rim, a loop handle.
Press or mould the edge with a feather or a shell, in a regular pattern of fine lines.
Pierce the wall with a punch for openwork baskets, in rows of small holes 3 to 4 mm wide.
Print or paint a pattern in a narrow band, and leave most of the surface plain.
Make the service in 50 or more shapes, so that a buyer can order any piece again.
anti_patterns: A white opaque tin glaze on a buff body
A modelled baroque relief with applied flowers
A deep ground colour with gold reserves

form.shape: Plain plates with a feather edge, covered tureens, oval platters, pierced baskets and sauceboats, in a strict classical outline.
form.profile: A clean circle with a flat rim and a shallow well; the rim carries a moulded shell edge, a bead or a plain band.
form.foot_and_rim: A low, plain foot with a glazed base; the rim is straight, with a moulded feather edge.
form.proportion: Plate diameter 22 to 25 cm and wall 3 to 4 mm thick; a service of 50 or more pieces.
rules: Keep the outline a plain circle or a strict oval.
Use one moulded edge on every plate in the service.
Keep the handle a simple loop or a plain knop.

bodies.rule: Use a light cream earthenware with a clear lead glaze, which is cheap and hard. Do not use porcelain: the style is the cheap, fine alternative.

methods: throwing and turning on the lathe
forming.joins: Handles are pressed in a mould and luted with slip; the knop is a plain ball or a small shell.
forming.details: A small tripod mark of the kiln stilts, a pale green pool of glaze in the foot, and the maker name stamped in the base.

glaze.pattern: Mostly plain; a feather-edge rim, a narrow band of enamel or a small printed scene or garland.
glaze.gloss: Soft gloss, about 60 to 80 GU, on a cream ground.
glaze.wear: The glaze crazes in a fine net over time and takes a brown tone in the cracks.

palette.strategy: A single cream tone, a pale yellow-green where the glaze pools, and a black or brown print for the narrow band.

firing.kiln: A coal-fired bottle kiln, with a biscuit firing at a high heat and a glaze firing at a lower heat.
processes: enamel or print firing at a low heat
firing.scale: Large factories at Burslem, Etruria and Leeds made it by the thousand, and sold it all over Europe and America.
firing.signs: Stilt marks, a faint cream tone, pale green pools of glaze, and the maker name stamped in the base.

pieces.form: Plate with a moulded feather edge and a clear cream glaze
Covered oval tureen with loop handles and a plain band of enamel
Pierced openwork basket on a stand, with holes in rows
Oval dish with a printed garland of leaves

positive: clear lead glaze, pale yellow cream

canonical_works.work: Queen's ware tea and dinner service for Queen Charlotte
Frog Service for Catherine the Great
Chestnut or orange basket, shape 32, first Queen's ware catalogue

evidence.title: Queen's ware teapot with enamel colours, c. 1775

emotion.target_response: A clean, sensible calm: the viewer sees a plain, even set and a few fine lines, and trusts that it is of good use.

use_cases: a plain period dinner service brief
a museum label on English earthenware
avoid_when: the brief wants a translucent porcelain
the brief needs a rich colour or gold
the brief wants a hand-made rustic look

modifiers.how: Change the body to bone china and add gilt bands and painted flowers.
Change the body to pearlware and print a blue Chinese-style pattern from a copper plate.
Keep the plain form, change the body to white porcelain, and drop the moulded edge.
